title: Does the VA Pay for Home Care? VA Community Care + Aid and Attendance, Explained
short_title: How veterans get home care through the VA
description: Two ways the VA can help pay for care at home: VA Community Care, where the VA arranges care and pays the provider directly, and Aid and Attendance, a monthly tax-free benefit for veterans and surviving spouses. Who qualifies, how to start, and what to gather.

parts.head: Does the VA pay for home care?
parts.sub: Two ways the VA can help, explained
parts.text: Does the VA pay for home care? For many veterans, it can. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions in Springfield. There are two main ways the VA can help pay for care at home, and I'll walk you through both.

parts.head: Community Care, and Aid and Attendance
parts.sub: The VA arranges care, or pays a monthly benefit
parts.text: The first is VA Community Care, where the VA arranges the care and pays the provider. The second is Aid and Attendance, a monthly cash benefit the veteran can use to help pay for care. Many families can use both.

parts.head: VA Community Care
parts.sub: The VA's network of approved local providers
parts.text: Let's start with Community Care. It's the VA's network of approved local providers. When the VA can't provide a needed service close enough or soon enough, a veteran can get that care from a community provider, and the VA pays the bill. Caring Companions is an approved provider in the VA Community Care Network.

parts.head: It starts with VA health care
parts.sub: Not enrolled yet? va.gov, by phone, or in person
parts.text: Home care through Community Care isn't something you apply for directly. It's arranged through the veteran's VA primary care team. If the veteran isn't enrolled in VA health care yet, that's step one. You can enroll at va dot gov, by phone, or in person.

parts.head: Ask the primary care team
parts.sub: "I need help with daily activities at home."
parts.text: Then schedule a visit with the VA primary care team and tell them directly: I need help with daily activities at home. Ask about home care through Community Care, and ask if Caring Companions can be your provider.

parts.head: Once it's approved, care starts
parts.text: Once the referral and authorization are in place, care can start, and the VA pays us directly. For service-connected care, there's no cost to the veteran. For other care, there may be a copay, depending on income.

parts.head: Aid and Attendance
parts.sub: A monthly, tax-free payment for care. Can add $1,400+ a month.
parts.text: Now, Aid and Attendance. It's a monthly, tax-free payment on top of a VA pension, for veterans or surviving spouses who need help with daily activities. The money is theirs to use as they choose, including for care at home. It can add over fourteen hundred dollars a month.

parts.head: Who qualifies
parts.sub: Wartime service, help with 2 daily activities, under the net worth limit
parts.text: To qualify, the veteran generally served during a wartime period, or is a surviving spouse who hasn't remarried. They need help with at least two daily activities. And their net worth has to be under the VA's yearly limit, about one hundred sixty-three thousand, seven hundred dollars in 2026. The home, one vehicle, and personal belongings don't count.

parts.head: Two things families miss
parts.sub: Care costs lower counted income. A 3-year look-back.
parts.text: Two things families often miss. Income is counted after subtracting what you already pay for care and medical costs, so many families who think they're over the limit actually qualify. And the VA looks back three years at assets given away below their value, which can cause a penalty.

parts.head: What to gather
parts.sub: DD-214, a doctor's form, statements, care receipts
parts.text: Here's what to gather: the DD-214 discharge papers, a doctor's exam form for Aid and Attendance, bank and income statements, and receipts for care and medical costs. Surviving spouses also need the marriage and death certificates.

parts.head: Applying
parts.sub: At va.gov, or with a veterans service officer. No cost.
parts.text: You can apply at va dot gov, or with help from a veterans service officer. There's no cost to apply.
Read our full guide at mo-care.com, or call us at (417) 234-8494. If you served, thank you. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions. Thanks for watching.
